column1: Which authentication method avoids storing API keys for supported Azure AI endpoint calls?
column2:
Managed Identity.
Azure manages the credentials for a managed identity and uses them to obtain access tokens. The application does not need to store an API key for supported identity-based calls. The target service must still grant that identity permission to invoke the model.
Review source

column1: What financial risk comes from unauthorized AI endpoint calls?
column2:
Unexpected charges from excessive API usage.
Model requests can consume billable resources even when the caller uses them without permission. A high request volume can therefore increase costs. Restrict who can invoke the endpoint and alert on unexpected usage.
Review source

column1: What confidentiality risk arises when SQL sends data to an external model endpoint?
column2:
Sensitive database content can leave the database in the request.
The request payload is the data sent to the model service. If it contains database text, that text leaves the database boundary. Encrypting the connection protects transport but does not authorize disclosure to the destination.
Review source

column1: Why restrict access to an endpoint serving a proprietary fine-tuned model?
column2:
To limit unauthorized probing of the model's behavior.
A fine-tuned model can reflect proprietary training or business behavior. Repeated unauthorized queries can reveal information about that behavior. Restrict endpoint access and monitor use rather than treating the model URL as sufficient protection.
Review source

column1: Which transport does sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint require to protect communication?
column2:
HTTPS with TLS encryption.
HTTPS encrypts the connection with TLS, which protects traffic in transit. The procedure does not support plain HTTP endpoints. The service still needs authentication and permissions to decide whether to accept the request.
Review source

column1: Where do you enable the logical server's system-assigned identity for Azure SQL outbound calls?
column2:
On the Azure SQL logical server resource's Identity configuration.
The logical server is an Azure resource that hosts Azure SQL databases. Enable its system-assigned identity through Azure resource management, not by creating a SQL user. That identity can then receive access to the external service.
Review source

column1: Which property identifies the system-assigned identity in a server object returned by Get-AzSqlServer?
column2:
Identity.PrincipalId.
PrincipalId is the directory object ID of the managed identity. Azure role assignments use it to identify who receives access. It is not the same value as the model endpoint URL or the token's audience.
Review source

column1: Whose identity does Azure SQL use for a REST call with a logical-server Managed Identity credential?
column2:
The logical server's configured managed identity.
The outbound service sees the logical server's selected managed identity, not automatically the user who ran the SQL statement. SQL permission to invoke the call and Azure permission to use the service are separate. Grant each at the required scope.
Review source

column1: Which purpose-built Azure role permits Azure OpenAI inference without permission to manage model deployments?
column2:
Cognitive Services OpenAI User.
Inference means calling a deployed model to obtain an output. Cognitive Services OpenAI User permits this use without model-deployment management rights. Assigning a broader management role is unnecessary when the caller only needs inference.
Review source

column1: Which Azure RBAC scope limits an identity's role assignment to one Azure OpenAI resource?
column2:
That Azure OpenAI resource.
A role assignment applies at its selected Azure resource scope. Assigning it to one Azure OpenAI resource avoids extending it across the whole resource group or subscription. The role and its scope together determine the identity's access.
Review source

column1: Which SQL object holds authentication configuration for an external REST call?
column2:
A database-scoped credential.
A database-scoped credential stores the authentication configuration used for an external resource. The REST procedure selects it through @credential. It is not the same as the database user's permissions or the external service's role assignment.
Review source

column1: Which credential IDENTITY value selects managed-identity authentication for an Azure SQL REST call?
column2:
'Managed Identity'.
This IDENTITY string tells SQL to obtain a token through the configured managed identity. It does not create that identity or grant service access. The called service must accept the token and authorize the identity.
Review source

column1: What does resourceid specify in a Managed Identity REST credential's SECRET JSON?
column2:
The token's target resource, or audience.
The token audience is the service the token is intended for. resourceid names that service when SQL requests a token. It is not the managed identity's principal ID, despite the word 'id'.
Review source

column1: Which token audience does the Azure OpenAI example use in a SQL Managed Identity REST credential?
column2:
https://cognitiveservices.azure.com
https://cognitiveservices.azure.com identifies the target service for the access token. The request URL separately identifies your particular resource and deployment. An audience is therefore not a replacement for the endpoint address.
Review source

column1: How must a credential name relate to the URL used by sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint?
column2:
A valid URL matching the request's scheme, host, and permitted path scope.
The credential name is a URL that limits where the credential can be used. Its scheme and host must match, and its path must cover the requested path. Do not use a friendly alias or include a query string in the credential name.
Review source

column1: Which system stored procedure sends an HTTPS request from supported SQL platforms?
column2:
sys.sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint.
This system procedure sends a request to an HTTPS endpoint from supported SQL platforms. A controlled application procedure can call it with approved destinations and inputs. Merely wrapping the call does not configure all required SQL and service permissions.
Review source

column1: What is the minimum SQL Server version that includes sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint?
column2:
SQL Server 2025 (17.x).
The SQL Server product first includes this procedure in SQL Server 2025. It is disabled by default there until the server configuration enables it. Azure SQL Database and Fabric SQL database have their own supported service behavior.
Review source

column1: Which sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint parameter specifies the destination URL?
column2:
@url.
@url supplies the actual HTTPS address to call, including the required path and query parameters. @credential separately chooses authentication. This invocation does not require a CREATE EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE object.
Review source

column1: Which sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint parameter selects authentication stored in a database-scoped credential?
column2:
@credential.
@credential names the existing database-scoped credential. Its URL-based name must cover the request URL under the matching rules. Selecting it does not grant missing permissions on the target service.
Review source

column1: Which T-SQL expression constructs an input JSON object from @InputText?
column2:
JSON_OBJECT('input': @InputText)
JSON_OBJECT constructs a valid JSON object from the supplied key and value. The literal key is input, and @InputText supplies its value. This avoids manually assembling JSON text around the input.
Review source

column1: How do you pass JSON_OBJECT output as @payload in a T-SQL stored-procedure call?
column2:
Store the result in a local variable, then pass the variable.
First assign the JSON result to a variable, such as @payload. Then pass @payload to EXECUTE. T-SQL does not accept this inline function call as the stored-procedure argument expression.
Review source

column1: How do you capture sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint's response in a local variable?
column2:
@response = @response OUTPUT.
Declare a local nvarchar(max) variable and pass it with OUTPUT. For example, @response = @response OUTPUT returns the response document to that variable. The procedure's integer return code is separate from this document.
Review source

column1: Which T-SQL JSON function extracts an embedding array rather than a scalar value?
column2:
JSON_QUERY.
An embedding is an array of numbers representing content. JSON_QUERY extracts an entire JSON array or object. JSON_VALUE is for one scalar value, so it is not the correct choice for the whole embedding array.
Review source

column1: In SQL's wrapped Azure OpenAI embeddings response, which JSON path selects the first embedding array?
column2:
$.result.data[0].embedding
The SQL procedure places the endpoint's response body under result. Inside that body, data is an array and [0] selects its first entry. embedding selects the vector array within that entry.
Review source

column1: What does return code 0 mean for sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint?
column2:
The HTTP call completed with a 2xx status code.
The procedure uses 0 to report a completed HTTP request with a success status in the 200-299 range. It does not replace the real HTTP status with 0. Read the response document when the exact status matters.
Review source

column1: When an endpoint returns HTTP 403, what does sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint return?
column2:
403.
An HTTP 403 response means the server returned a forbidden result. The procedure returns that non-2xx code rather than automatically raising a SQL exception. A failure to make the HTTPS call at all follows the exception path instead.
Review source

column1: Where does sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint store the HTTP status code in its JSON response?
column2:
$.response.status.http.code
The response object contains HTTP metadata, while result contains the endpoint's response body. This path selects the actual HTTP code, such as 200 or 403. Do not log a fixed success code for every call.
Review source

column1: How must AI-call logging handle a SQL REST request that throws before any HTTP response arrives?
column2:
Record the failure through an appropriate error-handling path.
An exception can bypass statements placed after the REST call. An appropriate error-handling path must record the failure without inventing an HTTP response or success code. The log must distinguish transport failures from completed HTTP error responses.
Review source

column1: Which statement lets AIFeatureUsers execute dbo.GetEmbedding?
column2:
GRANT EXECUTE ON dbo.GetEmbedding TO AIFeatureUsers;
This grant permits members of AIFeatureUsers to call the named wrapper procedure. A wrapper is an application procedure that controls an underlying call. Its effective execution context still needs the REST-invocation and credential permissions required by that call.
Review source

column1: Which statement adds an existing database user app-service-identity to AIFeatureUsers?
column2:
ALTER ROLE AIFeatureUsers ADD MEMBER [app-service-identity];
The database user must already exist before ADD MEMBER can add it to the role. The role supplies permissions inside SQL, such as access to a wrapper procedure. It does not assign an Azure role on the model service.
Review source

column1: Which database permission is required for direct REST-procedure calls in Azure SQL Database and Fabric SQL database?
column2:
EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT.
This permission allows direct use of the SQL REST invocation feature. It is broader than EXECUTE on one approved wrapper procedure. Restrict direct grants if applications must use a controlled path to external services.
Review source

column1: Which permission allows a database principal to use a specific credential for REST invocation?
column2:
REFERENCES on that database-scoped credential.
REFERENCES permits use of the named database-scoped credential for the call. It does not itself permit REST invocation or grant service-side access. Those checks are separate layers of the request.
Review source

column1: Which auth_mode enables Microsoft Entra token authentication on an Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoint?
column2:
aad_token.
aad_token requires a Microsoft Entra access token for requests to the managed online endpoint. The token identifies the caller, and Azure permissions determine whether scoring is allowed. Kubernetes online endpoints do not support this mode.
Review source

column1: Which token resource identifies Azure Machine Learning online scoring rather than Azure resource management?
column2:
https://ml.azure.com/
Scoring means sending data to a deployed model for inference. Its token targets https://ml.azure.com/, the scoring service. A token for Azure resource management targets a different service and is not interchangeable.
Review source

column1: Which RBAC action authorizes scoring on an Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoint with aad_token authentication?
column2:
Microsoft.MachineLearningServices/workspaces/onlineEndpoints/score/action
An Azure role must include this action to permit scoring with aad_token authentication. The action is the permission being granted, not a role name or a token audience. Assign an appropriate role to the caller at the required scope.
Review source

column1: How can Azure SQL invoke an AI service whose hostname is outside the REST procedure's allowlist?
column2:
Expose it through a supported Azure API Management endpoint.
Azure SQL restricts which endpoint hostnames the REST procedure can call. A supported Azure API Management endpoint can provide an approved route to another service. Secure both SQL-to-API-Management and API-Management-to-service connections.
Review source

column1: Which additional resource needs secured identity-based access in a batch-inference workflow?
column2:
The storage holding the inference data.
Batch inference often reads input from storage and writes results back there. Endpoint permission alone does not grant access to those files. Authorize the identities that need the input and output storage as well.
Review source

column1: What does ORIGINAL_LOGIN() identify in an AI-call log?
column2:
The login that originally established the SQL session.
ORIGINAL_LOGIN() records the identity that established the SQL connection, even if execution context later changes. With a shared application login, many human users have the same value. Log trusted application-user context separately when individual attribution is required.
Review source

column1: Which T-SQL function records the current UTC datetime2 timestamp for an AI call?
column2:
SYSUTCDATETIME().
SYSUTCDATETIME() returns the current UTC time as datetime2. UTC provides a common basis for comparing events across environments. Use the same time basis when recording the start and end of a call.
Review source

column1: Which expression measures AI-call duration in milliseconds from @StartTime?
column2:
DATEDIFF(millisecond, @StartTime, SYSUTCDATETIME())
Set @StartTime to SYSUTCDATETIME() before invoking the service. DATEDIFF with millisecond counts the millisecond boundaries between that value and the current UTC time. It measures the interval, not the endpoint's HTTP status.
Review source

column1: What can a sudden spike in AI calls from one principal indicate?
column2:
A compromised identity or an application bug.
An unexpected increase can come from unauthorized use or from faulty application behavior such as repeated calls. The count alone does not prove which cause applies. Investigate the caller, timing, endpoint, and outcomes.
Review source

column1: Which credential IDENTITY supports API-key headers for an external embedding model in Fabric SQL database?
column2:
HTTPEndpointHeaders.
HTTPEndpointHeaders sends authentication values from the credential as request headers. An external embedding endpoint can use an api-key header this way. Fabric workspace membership does not automatically supply that external service credential.
Review source

column1: How do Fabric's prebuilt AI models authenticate callers?
column2:
Through Fabric authentication.
Fabric's integrated prebuilt AI services use the caller's Fabric authentication. This differs from bringing an external Azure OpenAI resource with its own access configuration. Do not assume that every model called from Fabric uses the same credentials.
Review source

column1: Where is usage of Fabric's prebuilt AI services billed?
column2:
Against Fabric capacity through the Copilot and AI meter.
The integrated AI requests consume Fabric capacity and appear under the Copilot and AI meter. Spark compute used to run a notebook is reported separately. An AI request is therefore not accounted for only by the notebook's compute usage.
Review source

column1: Which app monitors capacity consumption from Fabric's prebuilt AI services?
column2:
The Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app.
The Capacity Metrics app shows how workloads consume Fabric capacity. Inspect the Copilot and AI meter for integrated AI-service usage. This helps separate AI consumption from Spark compute charges.
Review source

column1: Who enables Copilot for Fabric SQL database through tenant settings?
column2:
A Fabric tenant administrator.
A tenant administrator controls the relevant Copilot tenant setting. Membership in a workspace does not replace that approval. Supported paid capacity and regional availability are additional requirements.
Review source
